title: Most Productive Humans of All Time
axis: output plus transferable daily method, NOT Pantheon HPI fame

scoring.output: 0 to 40, sheer documented volume of finished work
scoring.method: 0 to 40, how concrete and transferable the daily technique is
scoring.fit: 0 to 20, relevance to a knowledge worker being productive in their days

humans.name: Isaac Asimov
humans.method: Ran several books in parallel so a stall meant rotating projects, never blocking. Butt-in-chair daily discipline.
humans.source: It's Been a Good Life; I. Asimov: A Memoir

humans.name: Anthony Trollope
humans.output: 47 novels while a full-time postal official
humans.method: 250 words every 15 minutes, watch on the desk, 3 hours before work. Finished a novel mid-session, started the next on the same page.

humans.name: Stephen King
humans.method: A fixed daily word quota with zero exceptions, holidays and birthdays included.
humans.source: On Writing: A Memoir of the Craft

humans.name: Benjamin Franklin
humans.output: Printer, scientist, statesman, inventor across one life
humans.method: The dawn-to-dusk daily schedule (morning intention, nightly reckoning) and the 13-virtue weekly rotation tracker.

humans.name: Peter Drucker
humans.method: Manage time before tasks, organize around contribution not activity, do first things first one at a time.

humans.name: Thomas Edison
humans.method: Systematize invention: notebook everything, iterate relentlessly, treat failure as data.
humans.source: Edison: A Biography by Matthew Josephson; his lab notebooks
humans.landmines: SEVERE: business ruthlessness, the Tesla feud and publicity stunts. Gate onboarding.

humans.name: Cal Newport
humans.method: Scheduled deep-work blocks and ruthless elimination of shallow work.

humans.name: Winston Churchill
humans.output: ~43 books, Nobel in Literature, ran a war
humans.method: Work from bed at dawn, a disciplined afternoon nap, then work late. A fixed daily rhythm sustained enormous output.
humans.source: My Early Life; the war memoirs
humans.landmines: SEVERE: colonial record, the Bengal famine. Gate onboarding.

humans.name: Ryan Holiday
humans.output: A book a year, prolific young
humans.method: The notecard research system: one idea per index card, filed by theme, compounding into books.
humans.source: Perennial Seller; his notecard-method essays and talks

humans.name: Johann Sebastian Bach
humans.output: ~1,100 works, a cantata a week for years
humans.method: A relentless weekly delivery cadence. Ship on schedule, do not wait for the muse.
humans.source: Johann Sebastian Bach: The Learned Musician by Christoph Wolff

humans.name: Leonhard Euler
humans.method: Total equanimity. Produced amid noise and children, and after losing his sight, by holding the work in his head.
humans.source: Leonhard Euler biographies; Dunham's Euler: The Master of Us All

humans.name: Tim Ferriss
humans.output: 5 books plus the definitive performance podcast
humans.method: 80/20 on everything, batch similar work, define the single most important thing.
humans.source: The 4-Hour Workweek; Tools of Titans; the podcast

humans.name: James Clear
humans.output: Atomic Habits, 20M+ copies, plus a weekly newsletter
humans.method: Systems over goals, the 1% daily improvement, habit stacking, make it obvious and easy.
humans.source: Atomic Habits; the 3-2-1 newsletter and talks

humans.name: Theodore Roosevelt
humans.output: 35+ books, president, rancher, explorer, all in 60 years
humans.method: Compartmentalized attention (total absorption in one task, then a clean switch) plus the strenuous-life energy discipline.
humans.source: The Autobiography of Theodore Roosevelt; Morris's trilogy
humans.landmines: SEVERE: imperialism and the racial views of his era. Gate onboarding.

humans.name: Paul Erdos
humans.output: ~1,500 papers, the most of any mathematician
humans.method: Monomaniacal single-subject focus plus radical collaboration, living out of a suitcase to work with everyone.
humans.source: The Man Who Loved Only Numbers by Paul Hoffman
humans.landmines: CAUTION: amphetamine use must not be valorized. The transferable lesson is the focus and collaboration, not the stimulants.

humans.name: Pablo Picasso
humans.method: Show up to the studio every day and treat sheer volume as the path. Low transferability, included to prove the thesis.
humans.source: A Life of Picasso by John Richardson
humans.landmines: SEVERE: personal conduct, treatment of the women in his life. Gate onboarding.

buildOrder: Trollope, Asimov, Drucker: historical track, purest daily methods, mostly public domain or cheap, no video needed
Franklin productivity skill: zero corpus cost, already grounded
Cal Newport and James Clear: prove the modern youchop track end to end

corpusTracks.historical: book is the corpus, use pdf-to-markdown and Gutenberg/archive.org, youchop does NOT apply
corpusTracks.modern: youchop.app extracts YouTube transcripts, plus their books
